subject: Short-notice fractional capacity fallback — actions & verification
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: April Chen <april.chen@acme-corp.com>, platform-ops@acme-corp.com
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 02:12:00 +0000
Subject: Short-notice fractional capacity fallback — actions & verification

Hi April —

We observed a fast-moving degradation in a small subset of inference requests affecting long-sequence workloads in the US region. To prevent error amplification while we stabilize the runtime, we've activated a fractional-capacity fallback on the affected pool. This routes 20% of traffic to a lower-latency, lower-memory variant with conservative KV prefetching.

What we did (short):
- Enabled fractional fallback at 02:05 UTC for pool us-west-prod-3
- Applied a temporary KV prefetch cap and conservative batching profile
- Enabled additional tracing to capture edge-case tokenization failures

What we need from Acme:
1) Please confirm if you observed increased 5xx rates or truncated outputs between 01:50–02:15 UTC.
2) If you have critical in-flight workloads, reply and we can pin those requests to the non-fallback path for 30 minutes while we validate the fix.

Attachments: fallback_activation_playbook.md (playbook), safeguard-rollout-checklist.txt

I'm standing by for your confirmation; we'll keep the fallback active until we complete validation (~2h target).

— Marissa
Marissa Cole | Sr. Incident Lead, Redwood Inference
From: April Chen <april.chen@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: platform-ops@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 02:23:41 +0000
Subject: Re: Short-notice fractional capacity fallback — actions & verification

Thanks Marissa —

We did see a spike in truncated outputs and a ~12% bump in 5xx for our batch jobs between 01:52 and 02:08 UTC. A few customer-facing long-form generation tasks failed mid-stream. Nothing mission-critical in-flight now — you can proceed with verification.

Can you confirm whether the fallback changes tokenization behavior for our current model version? We want to ensure post-processing still matches our validation harness.

— April
April Chen | Engineering Manager, Platform Integrations — Acme Corp
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 02:45:12 +0000
Subject: RE: Short-notice fractional capacity fallback — actions & verification

Quick internal notes / action items:
- Karthik: run the regression harness against fallback variant with Acme's longest prompt set (INF-7123) and report tokenization diffs within 30m. Use the attached checklist.
- Sean: keep the fallback pinned at 20% until we get OK from Acme or until 04:15 UTC. If errors drop below baseline for 30m, start gradual rollback to 0% over 15m.
- Marissa: keep April and platform-ops updated every 15m with concrete metrics (5xx count, avg latency P95, truncated-output rate).

Note: We've prioritized no model changes — fallback is purely serving-path and KV prefetch limits. Tokenization should be unchanged, but Karthik should verify end-to-end UUIDs for pre-tokenized inputs.

— Logan
Logan Wright | Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, April Chen <april.chen@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 04:20:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Short-notice fractional capacity fallback — actions & verification

Update — verification complete:

Summary:
- Ran regression harness against fallback variant w/ Acme prompt set (INF-7123) and 48 sample long prompts. No tokenization diffs detected (UUIDs matched).
- 5xx rate on Acme traffic dropped from 11.8% -> 1.7% within 18 minutes of activation.
- Truncated-output events for long-form tasks reduced by ~92%.
- Latency P95 on the fallback variant is +60ms on average compared to baseline; within the tolerated window for Acme per their SLOs.

Next steps (we executed):
- Left fallback at 20% for an additional 45 minutes to gather stability metrics.
- Prepared rollback play (gradual 5% decrements) if no regression appears in the next 30 minutes.

Attached checklist executed: safeguard-rollout-checklist.txt

April — based on the verification above, we recommend keeping the fallback for 30–45 more minutes and then beginning a controlled rollback beginning at 04:45 UTC if metrics remain healthy. If you prefer, we can keep the fallback longer while we complete a deeper root-cause analysis.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
